llm.summary: This paid skill is not clearly malicious, but it stores and sends sensitive order, question, and payment-credential data with inconsistent disclosure and limited user control.

dimensions.detail: Network access and local order files are coherent for a paid service, but sending the full question and payment credential to api.ideaidea.com.cn and storing full order data are high-trust actions for a legal/compliance-style query.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no separate installer, but the skill declares network, credential, filesystem read/write permissions and tells the agent to use or install the clawtip skill for payment processing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow is scoped to a three-stage payment flow, but it instructs automatic order creation and credential verification without an explicit per-run consent step, and SKILL.md contradicts itself about whether the user question is persistently stored.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Order files are written under ~/.openclaw/skills/orders/ and include the full question and payment-related fields; the artifacts provide no TTL, deletion flow, encryption, or restrictive file-permission handling.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is software IP lifecycle self-assessment, but the executable code mainly creates an order and verifies payment; service.py prints payment verification status and does not visibly deliver the promised assessment content.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending your question and payment credential/order data to api.ideaidea.com.cn and having full order metadata stored locally. Avoid putting confidential source details, credentials, or sensitive business facts in the question, and consider deleting local order files after use. The current scripts do not appear to upload source code or personal files, but they also do not visibly produce the advertised assessment result beyond payment verification.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The payment flow is expected for a paid skill, but the artifact-backed executable behavior appears to be payment/order authorization rather than the advertised assessment service.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The review-fixes document's auditor-focused language is not runtime behavior by itself, but it is relevant context and reduces confidence in the disclosure posture.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The suggested documentation tightening in the review-fixes document does not add enforceable runtime controls in the current scripts.
[SDI-4] unexpected: SKILL.md says questions are not persistently stored, while the workflow, data-handling section, and create_order.py store the question in the local order JSON.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending the user's question to the remote order API is disclosed and related to order creation, but there is no runtime confirmation or minimization beyond asking for the question argument.
[SQP-2] expected: Local order persistence is part of the disclosed payment flow, but the full question is retained without retention controls or local protection requirements.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending order number and payCredential to the remote service is expected for payment verification and is partly disclosed, but it happens automatically once service.py is run.
